# GIS MCP Server

> GIS MCP is an open-source Model Context Protocol server for GIS/geospatial analysis and AI agents.

Install with `pip install gis-mcp`. Default transport is STDIO (`gis-mcp`).
HTTP and SSE are also supported (`/mcp` or `/sse`; storage at `/storage`).
Docker serves HTTP on port 9010. Optional extras: `[visualize]`,
`[administrative-boundaries]`, `[climate]`, `[ecology]`, `[movement]`,
`[land-cover]`, `[satellite-imagery]`, `[gcp]`.

GIS MCP exposes Shapely, GeoPandas, Rasterio, PyProj, and PySAL as MCP
tools so agents run real geospatial operations instead of invented math.

## Start here

- [Home](https://gis-mcp.com/): Open-source MCP server that connects GIS libraries (Shapely, PyProj, GeoPandas, Rasterio, PySAL) to LLMs.
- [Getting started](https://gis-mcp.com/getting-started/): This guide helps you install and run the GIS MCP Server quickly using pip (with uv) and shows how to connect it to your IDE/client.
- [Architecture](https://gis-mcp.com/architecture/): This page explains where GIS MCP Server sits in agentic AI apps and how the server is structured inside. Diagrams live here (not in the GitHub README) so the docs stay the place...
- [Install](https://gis-mcp.com/install/): Pick the path that matches your setup:

## GIS AI agents

- [GIS AI agent overview](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/): Build AI agents that perform real geospatial work by connecting an agent framework to GIS MCP Server.
- [Agent architecture](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/architecture/): This page describes how GIS-enabled agents use GIS MCP Server. For the server’s internal components (tool modules, storage adapters, transports), also see the project Architectu...
- [Choosing a framework](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/choosing-framework/): GIS MCP Server is framework-agnostic: any runtime that can act as an MCP client can call its tools. This page helps you pick a tutorial path and avoid frameworks that are a poor...
- [Best practices](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/best-practices/): Guidance for building reliable agents on top of GIS MCP Server. Practices below assume the current product model: GIS MCP exposes MCP tools; your agent framework owns planning,...
- [LangChain park-buffer agent](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/langchain/basic-geospatial-agent/): Build a small LangChain agent that uses GIS MCP Server tools to answer a real planning question: *does a proposed building fall within 100 meters of a park?*
- [LangGraph stateful agent](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/langgraph/stateful-geospatial-agent/): Build a stateful LangGraph pipeline that answers: *is a school within a 400 m walking buffer of a transit stop?*
- [LangGraph multi-agent workflow](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/langgraph/multi-agent-geospatial-workflow/): A practical three-agent LangGraph pipeline for a river setback compliance check. Agents have separated jobs; only one of them calls GIS MCP.
- [LangGraph file-based site suitability](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/langgraph/file-based-site-suitability/): A layer-based LangGraph pattern on GIS MCP: clip → overlay → CRS-safe buffer → spatial join → map.
- [OpenAI Agents SDK (Node.js)](https://gis-mcp.com/gis-ai-agent/openai-nodejs/basic-geospatial-agent/): Welcome! This tutorial will guide you on setting up the gis-mcp server and building a Node.js agent that can perform geospatial operations.

## API overviews

- [Data gathering](https://gis-mcp.com/data-gathering/): This section explains how to fetch external datasets with GIS-MCP. Currently covered:
- [Shapely](https://gis-mcp.com/api/shapely/): High-level geometric operations exposed via MCP. All tools accept and return geometries as WKT strings.
- [PyProj](https://gis-mcp.com/api/pyproj/): Coordinate reference system utilities and geodetic calculations.
- [GeoPandas](https://gis-mcp.com/api/geopandas/): I/O and attribute-join helpers for vector data.
- [Rasterio](https://gis-mcp.com/api/rasterio/): Raster I/O, processing, and analysis.
- [PySAL](https://gis-mcp.com/api/pysal/): Spatial autocorrelation and clustering tools powered by PySAL/ESDA.
- [Visualization](https://gis-mcp.com/api/visualize/): The visualization module provides tools for creating both static and interactive maps from geospatial data. This module requires the [visualize] extra to be installed.
